title: PipelineForge Config (converted from .pfcfg)
description: One converted entry config. Includes are flattened at conversion time into a single, ordered 'assignments' list (static merge list). Conditionals and interpolation are kept dynamic and resolved by the evaluator at read time, against a given environment.

entry.description: Path to the original entry .pfcfg file, relative to starter/configs/.

sources.description: Every .pfcfg file flattened into this JSON, in the order they were merged (provenance only — not required for evaluation).

assignments.description: Every key = value assignment encountered during textual macro-expansion of the include tree, in original textual order. Multiple entries may share the same section/key (e.g. one default, one conditional override) — the evaluator applies them in order, letting later assignments whose condition passes overwrite earlier ones. This is what makes last-write-wins possible without JSON key collisions.

referenced_env_vars.description: Optional. Every environment variable name referenced anywhere in this config's assignments, via @ifdef/@ifndef conditions or ${VAR...} interpolation. $(section.key) cross-references are excluded (they aren't env vars). Auto-extracted by the converter; used to auto-generate test environments for verification without a human having to read the file first.

section.description: Dotted section path, exactly as in the original [section] header.

key.description: The key name within the section.

value.description: Raw value string, unresolved. May contain ${VAR}, ${VAR:-default}, ${VAR:+alt}, or $(section.key) interpolation syntax, re-parsed by the evaluator at read time. List values remain comma-joined strings (e.g. 'compile,test,build'), not JSON arrays.

origin.description: Where this assignment came from in the original .pfcfg tree, for debugging and the unmigratable report.

order.description: Monotonically increasing position of this assignment in the fully-expanded, textual, top-to-bottom token stream. Used by the evaluator to break ties when more than one candidate's condition passes for the same section.key: highest passing order wins. Assignments must be emitted by the converter with order values matching their true textual sequence across the flattened include tree.

condition.description: Null when the assignment is unconditional. Otherwise a single ifdef/ifndef check, or a conjunction of nested conditions (for nested @ifdef/@ifndef blocks).

type.description: ifdef: true when var is set and non-empty in the environment. ifndef: true when var is unset or empty.

all.description: All nested conditions must pass. Represents nested @ifdef/@ifndef blocks (an assignment inside two wrapping conditionals).
